\section{Two counting pathologies we had to fix}
\label{app:pathologies}

Both errors below were made by us and are recorded because a reader reproducing this census will hit them.

\paragraph{Substring matching contaminates shell groups.} Grouping the corpus by a substring test on the opening sentence silently admits the shell 'framed item on a plain wall in a quiet museum study room', which is a different opening that passes at a different rate. The contaminated group, 2 distinct openings merged, reports 175/176 = 99.4\%; the longest single exact match is 161/161 = 100.0\%. \textbf{Group by the complete sentence, never by a substring.}

\paragraph{Truncating the key merges distinct pose clauses.} Using a 200-character prefix as the grouping key merges clauses that differ after the cut. Under truncation the corpus yields 55 distinct clauses, of which 15 have a usable denominator; with the full key it yields 75 and 22. Truncation also produced a self-contradictory reading---one key reporting both 0/2 and 152/164---which is how the error was found.

\paragraph{Reading only one field loses refusals.} Early batch scripts wrote the error text to a field named body; later ones use err. Reading only err classifies 147 of the 185 refusals as empty. The correct count of empty refusals is 31. \textbf{Read every plausible field.}

\paragraph{The machine-readable code merges four things.} The code field \texttt{content\_policy\_violation} is returned for content-policy refusals, for named-character refusals, and for rate-limit messages. A count built on that field therefore mixes a scheduling event with a policy decision.
